nodes.rationale: Required for regulatory compliance, ops debugging, and SLA dispute resolution. Any correction is a new record pointing to the old one.

nodes.label: Nightly Stability — Grids and Routes Replan Once Nightly
nodes.rationale: Intraday changes create chaos; nightly stability preferred with human approval for exceptions.

nodes.label: Cron-Meeting Hard Constraint
nodes.rationale: M5 must confirm parcel reaches hub cron before airline cutoff — no assignment otherwise. Ensures SLA feasibility.

nodes.label: DA Utilisation ~70% Cost Floor
nodes.rationale: 70% shift engaged, 30% idle. Do not optimise purely for speed — this is the cost floor in M3, M5, M6.

nodes.label: XC-D-001 Event Transport: Kafka Async, HTTP Sync
nodes.rationale: Kafka decouples producers and consumers. When a module is extracted into its own service, no code changes needed — only deployment changes. Database polling degrades under load.

nodes.label: XC-D-002 Append-Only Audit Trail Decision
nodes.rationale: Required for regulatory compliance, ops debugging, and SLA dispute resolution.

nodes.label: XC-D-007 Technology Stack: Java 21, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL, Kafka
M4-D-001 B2B and B2C Use Separate API Endpoints
nodes.rationale: A single endpoint with customerType switch creates complex branching and leaks B2B concepts into B2C contract. Separate endpoints are independently versioned.

nodes.label: M4-D-002 B2C Payment via Razorpay Prepaid
M4-D-005 ETA Computation Entirely Owned by M9
M4-D-016 Booking Endpoint Idempotency
nodes.rationale: Network retries and double-taps are inevitable. Without idempotency, Razorpay capture could succeed while DB write fails, leaving customer charged without a shipment.

nodes.label: M4-D-017 B2B Credit Check Atomicity via SELECT FOR UPDATE
nodes.rationale: Concurrent B2B bookings from same account could race past credit limit check. Row-level locking serialises them.

nodes.label: M4-D-018 Resilience4j Circuit Breakers on Synchronous Calls
M4-D-019 COD in v1 for B2C and C2C
M4-D-020 All Pricing Owned by M2
nodes.rationale: Clear separation of concerns. Pricing rules change frequently. Having any pricing logic in M4 creates drift and debugging confusion.

nodes.label: M8-D-001 QR Code Barcode Format
nodes.rationale: DA app uses phone cameras for scanning; QR natively supported by modern phones without dedicated hardware. Risk: airport/GHA scanners may expect IATA standard.

nodes.label: BD-001 Cancellation Policy — Pending Business Decision
RabbitMQ — Async Event Transport
nodes.rationale: Cheap, push-based (low latency), simple. Migrated from Kafka 2026-06-17. Accepted trade-off: publish-direct means crash between DB-commit and publish can lose an event.

nodes.label: Ports-and-Adapters for Messaging — Broker Abstraction
nodes.rationale: Business code depends only on EventPublisher and EventHandler. The broker lives behind them. Future broker swap is an adapter change — zero business-code change.

C2C Self-Registration — Public Endpoint Auto-Login
nodes.rationale: C2C individuals ship personal parcels; no commercial pre-conditions. Friction at signup loses customers. B2C/B2B require admin approval because service agreement and rate setup needed.

nodes.label: Stateless Sessions — No Refresh Token Design Decision
nodes.rationale: Stateless (no server-side session) simplifies horizontal scaling. No refresh token — re-login at shift-change is natural boundary. API keys for long-running machine integrations.

nodes.label: Permission Strings Fixed at Code Time — No Runtime Addition
nodes.rationale: A misconfigured permission is a production incident and should go through code review and automated tests. Adding a new action requires code change, migration, and deploy.

nodes.label: M1 Open Question: DA Login Method
M1 Open Question: Overnight Session Expiry
City-Scoped Role Constraint
nodes.rationale: City-scoped roles (STATION_MANAGER, SUPERVISOR, HUB_OPERATOR, DELIVERY_ASSOCIATE, VAN_DRIVER, CRON_DRIVER, CALL_CENTER_AGENT) require cityId to prevent cross-city data access. Non-city-scoped roles (ADMIN, B2B_USER, B2C_CUSTOMER, C2C_CUSTOMER, AIRLINE_GHA) skip the city check.

nodes.label: JWT Filter Chain Decision Tree
nodes.rationale: Filter always calls filterChain.doFilter() even on failure — leaves SecurityContext empty rather than short-circuiting. This allows the framework to return 403 for protected endpoints rather than a direct 401 in the filter.

nodes.label: C2C Customer Self-Registration Flow
nodes.rationale: C2C allows self-registration (no admin required) because individuals have no commercial pre-conditions. B2C and B2B require admin-created accounts due to service agreements and negotiated rates.

nodes.label: Append-Only Role Audit Log
nodes.rationale: role_audit_logs is append-only — no DELETE or UPDATE path. FK-free (stores UUID strings, not FK references) so audit rows survive even if actor/target accounts are deleted.

nodes.label: Account Deactivation Takes Effect on Next Request
nodes.rationale: JWT filter re-checks active=true from DB on every request. Deactivation takes effect immediately on next request even if JWT is still valid. Role changes do NOT take effect until next login (stateless JWT trade-off).

nodes.label: M2 Weight Slab Pricing Model
nodes.rationale: Base covers first 0.5kg slab. Each additional 0.5kg slab decays 10pp, floored at 60%. Formula: pct(n) = max(60, 100 - 10*(n-1)). Designed so heavy parcels pay more but not linearly.

nodes.label: Rate Card Append-Only Versioning
nodes.rationale: rate_card rows are never mutated. Publishing a new version inserts a fresh ACTIVE row and flips the prior ACTIVE card to SUPERSEDED. Shipment stores rateCardVersion for historical reconciliation.

nodes.label: M2 Per-Parcel Cost Floor Model
nodes.rationale: floor = da_share + van_share + hub_cost + airline_cost. da_share divides by effective capacity (nameplate × 70% utilisation) so DA utilisation target raises the floor — consistent with M3/M5/M6 cost floor invariant.

nodes.label: Pricing Circuit Breaker (NoRateConfiguredException excluded)
nodes.rationale: NoRateConfiguredException is excluded from the pricing circuit breaker because a missing rate is a business outcome, not a system failure. Repeated unpriced-lane attempts should not trip the breaker and 503 priced lanes.

nodes.label: StubPricingAdapter Removal (real adapter all profiles)
nodes.rationale: StubPricingAdapter deleted from app module; PricingPortAdapter now active in all profiles including prod. The demo relies on seeded local/dev DB rows existing.

nodes.label: M3 Algorithm Decision: CP-SAT with Lazy Cuts
Lazy Cuts Contiguity Approach
nodes.rationale: Lazy cuts chosen over flow-based spanning tree because flow-based requires O(K×N) additional variables upfront. Lazy cuts adds constraints only where violations actually occur. Convergence at ≤200 tiles/≤70 DAs: 2-5 rounds, under 30 seconds total.

nodes.label: OsrmMatrixRefreshJob (monthly, 02:00 IST 1st)
nodes.rationale: tile_travel_time is the only table replaced wholesale on refresh (not append-only). All other M3 tables are append-only.

nodes.label: DaRosterPort Interface (NoOpDaRosterPort placeholder)
nodes.rationale: Port pattern keeps M1 dependency explicit and swappable. NoOpDaRosterPort returns empty list + WARN log until M1 ships a real RealDaRosterPort annotated @Primary.

nodes.label: CP-SAT Flow + Load Balance Infeasibility (peripheral seeds)
Two-Phase CP-SAT Solve (Phase 1 load + Phase 2 BFS repair)
nodes.rationale: Key insight: load balance and connectivity are separate problems and should be solved separately in sequence. Phase 1: CP-SAT without flow constraints (always feasible). Phase 2: BFS repairs disconnected tiles by reassigning to adjacent DA with most remaining capacity.

nodes.label: M4DataLoader REQUIRES_NEW Transaction Isolation
nodes.rationale: M4 SQL queries wrapped in REQUIRES_NEW transactions so that when shipment_leg_events doesn't exist, the inner transaction rolls back without corrupting the outer transaction (was causing UnexpectedRollbackException).

nodes.label: M3 Fixed 2km×2km Rectangular Tile Geometry
nodes.rationale: Rectangular tiles chosen for: operational legibility (street names), simple O(1) adjacency math, index-based GPS lookup, grid vertex alignment with M6 van routes, Indian city block patterns.

nodes.label: H3 vs Rectangular Tile Shape Comparison
H3 CP-SAT Model Size Penalty (5x larger at res-8)
nodes.rationale: H3 resolution 8 (closest to 2km) produces ~810 nodes vs ~150 for rectangular tiles — 5x larger CP-SAT model for identical output quality. No H3 resolution cleanly maps to 2km without this penalty.

nodes.label: H3 Flyway Migration Strategy (V11–V17 new tables)
nodes.rationale: V1–V10 stay on disk untouched. V11–V17 create new h3_* prefixed tables. Old tables become inert reference data. This avoids corrupting flyway_schema_history on all environments.

nodes.label: M3 Append-Only Table Invariant
nodes.rationale: da_hex_assignment, assignment_proposal, assignment_proposal_region, h3_hex_vertex are append-only. Only h3_hex_travel_time is replace-in-place on monthly OSRM refresh.

nodes.label: Uber H3 + DISCO Batch Matching Architecture
Async Lifecycle Producers Gap (M5/M6/M7/M8/M9/M11 not built)
nodes.rationale: All post-BOOKED state transitions require Kafka events from M5-M11 which are not yet built. Without producers, M4's state machine never advances past BOOKED. The demo must use event injection simulation for Tier 3 flows.

nodes.label: In-process ApplicationEvent Decoupling Seam
nodes.rationale: The state machine and booking flow stay ignorant of Kafka. They publish in-process Spring ApplicationEvents; ShipmentEventProducer listens with @TransactionalEventListener(AFTER_COMMIT) and emits to Kafka. This guarantees no event fires for a rolled-back DB change.

nodes.label: M4 Phase 0: Shared Contracts in common module
DTD-10-A: ETA Network Call Inside DB Transaction (Critical Bug)
nodes.rationale: EtaPort.fetchEta() is an outbound network call to M9 that executes inside the TransactionTemplate.execute() callback, holding a DB connection open for the full round-trip. Under concurrent bookings this exhausts the connection pool. Fix: extract ETA from persist(), call after TX commits.

nodes.label: DTD-10-B: IdempotencyFilter Imports auth Internal Class
nodes.rationale: IdempotencyFilter imports com.oneday.auth.security.AuthUserDetails, violating the cross-module boundary rule. Fix: define OneDayPrincipal interface in common; have AuthUserDetails implement it; IdempotencyFilter depends only on common.

nodes.label: M4 Event Routing Table (all module → state transitions)
RabbitMQ Transport (not Kafka) for M5 Events
nodes.rationale: M5 messaging was refactored from Kafka to RabbitMQ. KafkaTopics.java → EventStreams.java (RabbitMQ topic exchanges). Producers use EventPublisher.publish(stream, event); consumers use @RabbitListener. The event-driven design is unchanged, only the transport differs.

nodes.label: da_status DB Table (one row per DA, in-memory authoritative)
M5 Design Review Critical Bugs (4 items)
Partial Unique Index Fix for dispatch_queue Rescheduled Pickups
nodes.rationale: A table-level UNIQUE(da_id, shipment_id, task_type, operating_date) on dispatch_queue breaks rescheduled pickups: after PICKUP_FAILED → PICKUP_RESCHEDULED, M5 idempotency guard finds the existing FAILED row and skips it. Fix: partial unique index WHERE status NOT IN ('FAILED', 'CANCELLED').
